title: Roblox Excercises Conservative Revenue Recognition Policy
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA revisits Roblox after a $10-12 rise since his 31 July buy call. The title's point is accounting: Roblox spreads Robux deposits over 12-24 months while users spend them in days, so reported revenue is understated and losses overstated; on price to free cash flow (21x, near multi-year lows) he calls it undervalued, while his updated DCF of about $46 against $49.55 says fairly valued and just inside his margin of safety. Cost cuts doubled cash flow from operations to sales (15% to 37%) and revenue per employee rose to $1.76 million. He reiterates BUY, medium conviction — first tracked in this watch, no prior tracked stance.

calls.video_title: Roblox Excercises Conservative Revenue Recognition Policy
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated, medium conviction (his 31 Jul call, reiterated here; first tracked in calls.json, no flip): conservative revenue recognition (Robux spread over 12-24 months though kids spend it in days) understates revenue and overstates losses, so price/free-cash-flow at 21x — near its lowest in years — is the right lens and looks undervalued, even though his DCF (~$46 vs $49.55) says only fairly valued / just inside his 5-10% margin of safety.
calls.base_case: Cost cuts since late 2022 doubled CFO/sales from 15% to 37% and lifted revenue per employee from $1.2M to $1.76M; the developer revenue-share model keeps that leverage rising, helped by AI productivity.
calls.bull_case: Engagement keeps growing post-reopening, developer tools improve, and revenue per employee compounds further.
calls.bear_case: Still loss-making on reported numbers; on his own DCF there is little margin of safety at $49.55 after a $10-12 rise since July.
